extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, supervisory personnel (SPEs), and patent practitioners seeking to understand examiner decision process
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the USPTO examiner decision-making workflow: who may decide to allow or reject claims during first and second examination stages, and the structure/outcomes of the appeals process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final authority for patentability determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The final say for the determination of patentability resides with the Primary Examiner (MPEP §1004) with the exception when a Junior Examiner has partial signatory authority (MPEP §1005).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary Examiner is the deciding official on patentability. Junior Examiner may have partial signatory authority in limited circumstances per MPEP §1005; consult MPEP references for scope of partial signatory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision point: First Examination — deciding official and office action procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: During first examination: An examiner with signatory authority decides to reject or allow claims. An examiner without signatory authority prepares an Office action in which claims are rejected or allowed, and an examiner with signatory authority or SPE reviews, approves, and signs Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the preparing examiner lacks signatory authority, the Office action must be reviewed and signed by an examiner with signatory authority or the SPE before issuance. This establishes who may make the substantive decision versus who may draft the action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision point: Second Examination — post-response decision and office action procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If a compliant response is filed, then: An examiner with signatory authority decides to reject or allow claims. An examiner without signatory authority prepares an Office action in which claims are rejected or allowed, and an examiner with signatory authority or SPE reviews, approves, and signs Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The same decision/signing authority structure applies on second examination after a compliant response. The trigger for this stage is the filing of a compliant response by the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals initiation after two rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: If claims have been twice rejected, Applicant may appeal decision to PTAB by filing a notice of appeal and an appeal brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Twice-rejected claims permit appeal to the Patent Trial and Appeal Board; applicants must file the required notice and brief to initiate the appeal. Follow PTAB rules and deadlines for filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal conference composition and possible Office decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal conference is held with the examiner, SPE, and an additional conferee having sufficient experience to be of assistance in the consideration of the merits of the issues on appeal. The Office makes a decision to continue to re-open prosecution, allow claims, or proceed with the appeal. If a decision is made by the Office to proceed with the appeal, the examiner prepares an examiner’s answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The appeal conference convenes relevant decision-makers (examiner, SPE, experienced conferee) to choose among reopening prosecution, allowing claims, or advancing to formal appeal. If proceeding to appeal, the examiner is responsible for preparing the examiner’s answer as the next procedural step.
